messages.subject: mcmc::chains storage/access done
parts:
I finished the constructor, getters, and setters
for the mcmc::chains object. There's pretty
extensive doc (including read/write synch requirements
per object) and examples in the unit test.

At this point, Jiqiang should be able to start
creating the Rcpp wrapper for mcmc::chains so that the
getters will be accessible from R (and the constructor
and setters if we want it to be usable outside
of Stan, but otherwise the sampler will create the
chains object).

The other thing that needs to be done independently
of the sampler is implementing an io::var_context
extension for reading from R lists (if lists are indeed
how we're going to pass in variables -- do we
want to default so they get read out of the
top-level enviroment?).

I'm about to start rolling in the various methods
we need for means, etc. Some of them are just migrating
Daniel's implementations for single variables.

Then I'll add the functions we need to the compiled
model and make generating the main() method configurable
(we don't want it in the R interface).

I'd still appreciate a ref on how to apply FFT for
autocorrelation and variograms if anyone has one handy.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] mcmc::chains storage/access done
parts:
On 5/17/12 2:55 PM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> Thanks. I will start to use it soon.
>
> I have a rlist_var_context implemented
> http://code.google.com/p/stan/source/browse/rstan/rstan/inst/include/rlist_var_context.hpp?name=rstan

Nice. I'm SOOO glad you're doing the R side
of things. It looks like a lot of work.
> I just changed your dump's constructor.

That should work -- you're just copying in the
values from the list to the way I built the
data structures.

A more memory-efficient implementation would
be to hold a reference to the R list rather
than copying it into the data structures I used.
Then the gets read out of the list when they are called.

I implemented io::dump the way I did because I was
reading out of an ASCII stream (e.g., file), which doesn't
allow reasonable random access. From an R list, you
should be able to be lazy about when you get a value
and not have to copy everything.

I wouldn't worry about trying to change it now if
it works. Unless we have lots of data, it's not going
to be that much extra memory because it's in fairly
tight C++ std::vector instances. And the overall amount
of work won't be that much different (maybe two extra
copies -- into the temp and then back into the output).

>
> Then I'll add the functions we need to the compiled
> model and make generating the main() method configurable
> (we don't want it in the R interface).
>
> Technically, the main() seems not to be an issue though I
> do not like it in the R interface.

I agree that we don't want a global main() function potentially
polluting R's namespace. Even if we can get it to work
through Rcpp. It's no big deal to provide a flag to stanc
indicating whether or not to generate the main.

- Bob
